title: 90s Engineer Onboarding: Setup, Cost & Latency Frames for Hosted API
body:
Objective:
Quick internal brief to align on a compact, engineer-focused hosted API offer that highlights '90-second' integration, clear cost anchors, and latency-first language for demo and pricing pages. Intended to be lean and A/B testable.

Context / Why this: 
- Lots of existing assets emphasize 'fast onramp' but lean toward marketing copy. Engineering audiences want concrete, time-bound confidence: "I can wire this in 90s and measure cost/latency".
- Competitors skew either simplicity-only (abstract pricing) or enterprise-heavy (complex contracts). We can win mid-market + early-stage engineers by giving both speed and transparent economics.

Primary audience:
- Individual engineers/engineering teams evaluating an LLM hosted API for prototyping and early productization.
- Secondary: platform teams assessing integration effort and predictable unit economics.

Core developer-first value props (short lines for hero + bullets):
1) Ship in 90s — real integration time, not marketing fluff.
   - Copy: "90 seconds to your first token" / "Start generating in 90s"
   - Evidence: single curl + SDK snippet, no account setup blockers, immediate free trial credits.
2) Predictable unit economics by design
   - Copy: "Per-token pricing with visible cost per route" / "Estimate, simulate, deploy"
   - Evidence: sample invoice breakdown, token-level observability in Console.
3) Latency you can rely on
   - Copy: "<100ms p50 for chat completions on common prompts" (experiment-backed for selected models/regions)
   - Evidence: latency benchmark snippet, option to pin lower-latency variants (dedicated pools)
4) Built for production — fallbacks and QoS out of the box
   - Copy: "Graceful fallbacks when capacity shifts"
   - Evidence: routing policy example and small config snippet

Quickstart angles (activation flows to test):
A — 90s CLI/CURL path (primary):
  - One-liner curl that returns a completion in ~90s from account creation (include token placeholder).
  - Follow with minimal SDK snippet (5 lines) and a local trace showing latency and token count.
B — 5-min 'from playground to prod' (secondary):
  - Show route creation, cost estimate, small policy to pin model variant.
C — Cost-sim sandbox (experiment):
  - Upload demo prompt set, run cost estimate across model/quantization combos.

Pricing-language drafts (framing + sample microcopy):
- Headline anchor: "Pay per token. Predictable pricing. Start free."
- Short subline: "Metered usage, simple tiers — with optional reserved capacity for predictable throughput."
- Pay-as-you-go copy (FAQ style):
  - "How much will it cost? Estimate easily: 100 prompts * X tokens avg = Y unit cost. See calculator in Console."
- Free credits copy: "$200 starter credits — enough for ~10k short prompt tests."
- Reserved / Burst language: "Reserve baseline throughput for mission-critical apps. Burst capacity without overprovisioning."
- Savings hook: "Optimize tokens with suggested batching and prefix caching — expect up to 3x improvement in unit cost for chat-heavy workloads."

Competitive notes (quick scan):
- Major cloud LLM APIs: often present flat per-thousand-token rates but hide regional or model variant deltas. They lean on simplicity.
  - Opportunity: show token-level breakdown and a cost-sim sandbox to surface differences.
- Inference infra vendors (self-hosted runtimes): present cheaper unit costs at scale but require infra/time.
  - Opportunity: emphasize time-to-value + observability + simple path to Dedicated when scale justifies it.
- Startups focused on 'developer delight' claim <1 minute onboarding. We differentiate by adding concrete latency anchors + cost transparency.

Key claims to validate with data (action items):
- Average end-to-end 'first token' time for curl path across regions (want median and 95th). (owner: eng-ux)
- p50/p95 latency profiles for our curated models on hosted plan (owner: applied-ml)
- Typical token consumption for 10 sample quickstart prompts to set the free credit estimate (owner: product-hosted-api)
- Cost delta between default and recommended quantized variants for chat workloads (owner: optimize)

A/B test variants to run (copy + UX):
Variant 1 - Speed-first: "90s to first token" + small cost blurb
Variant 2 - Cost-first: "Estimate your bill in 30s" + speed blurb
Variant 3 - Reliability-first: "SLAs, reserved pools, and fallbacks" + speed and cost as secondary
Metrics: activation rate (90s curl success), time to first paid API call, demo -> paid conversion, support contact rate for onboarding.

Suggested page layout (for hosted-api quickstart landing):
- Hero: 90s claim + one-liner cost anchor + single-line CTA (Get started, claim credits)
- 3 columns: Code (curl + SDK), Price (micro-estimate + credits), Latency (p50/p95 numbers)
- Lower: cost-sim sandbox CTA + link to docs and to Dedicated contact form

Microcopy snippets (ready-to-use):
- CTA primary: "Get started — 90s to first token"
- Console tooltip for cost: "Estimate uses avg token length from your prompt set — results approximate."
- Error fallback message: "No compatible capacity in region — we rerouted to a compatible variant; latency may vary."

Open questions / tradeoffs: 
- Do we want to publish numeric latency guarantees for hosted tier, or only for Dedicated? (ops risk vs. product appeal)
- Free credit sizing: is $200 the right anchor? need finance input.
- How much model-level transparency can we show without overwhelming the quickstart?

Next steps / owners: 
- Prototype 90s curl flow with fresh credentials and record E2E times (owner: devexp / Liam).
- Create cost-sim playground mock (owner: product-hosted-api / Priya).
- Collate latency bench outputs and produce p50/p95 table (owner: applied-ml / Evelyn).
- Draft landing copy + 3 A/B variants for CRO to run (owner: go-to-market / Maya).

Notes to self / slack snippets: 
- Slack thread: #gtm-hosted-api — tag: @product-hosted-api, @devexp, @applied-ml
- Quick refs: confluence:HOSTED-quickstart, JIRA-3245

Rough timeline: 3 sprints to get data + prototypes ready for Q1 experiments.

Raw brainstorm lines (messy, keep):
- "90s" is a better engineer promise than "30s" because it's believable across regions.
- Consider a "cost shadow" overlay on the quickstart that follows the user as they type prompts.
- Offer a 'simulate my plan' modal that shows monthly bill based on usage histogram.

Comments welcome — add notes inline or ping me on Slack.
